name: v5.2.0
body:
## New Features

- Added DB2 support, with access through the web terminal and native client proxy
- Added dual-protocol connectivity for ClickHouse, supporting HTTP and Native connections to the same asset
- Added a single-endpoint proxy for Redis Cluster, with support for node routing and redirection
- Added SQL Server domain account authentication using NTLMv2 and Kerberos through managed domain accounts
- Expanded job execution support for Oracle, Dameng, OceanBase, DB2, ClickHouse, and other databases
- Expanded account automation capabilities for Dameng, OceanBase MySQL tenants, and ClickHouse
- Added a local Codex assistant to the desktop client
- Enhanced web session management with configurable login lifetimes, automatic renewal on requests, sign-out after all pages are closed, and automatic idle locking with password-based unlocking
- Enhanced desktop client session management with configurable maximum login lifetimes that are not extended by user activity, reauthentication on expiry, optional reauthentication after fully exiting and reopening the client, and automatic idle locking with password-based unlocking
- Added Tencent Cloud database asset synchronization for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server [JumpServer EE]
- Added visual approval workflows with multi-level approvals, conditional branching, all-approver and any-approver approval modes, approval reassignment, additional approvers, and timeout handling [JumpServer EE]
- Expanded ticket-based approvals to cover password viewing, account password changes, file uploads and downloads, and recording downloads [JumpServer EE]
- Added application credential rotation with alternating rotation between primary and standby accounts, account switching across assets, execution history, and client status reporting [JumpServer EE]
- Added OceanBase support for MySQL-compatible and Oracle-compatible tenants [JumpServer EE]

## Security Enhancements

- Enhanced the workbench with flexible split views, SSH input broadcasting, and customizable keyboard shortcuts
- Strengthened access control for scheduled jobs by applying the relevant access control policies at execution time
- Improved login lifetime enforcement and reauthentication after exit
- Strengthened desktop client site security with HTTPS certificate validation enabled by default, certificate details, site-specific certificate exceptions, and risk confirmation before accessing sites over HTTP
- Hardened automation execution with a dedicated SSH Ansible executor, safeguards against playbook path traversal, and restrictions on symbolic links, bundled configuration files, and plugins
- Strengthened API parameter validation and organization and role permission checks
- Expanded sensitive data masking in database query results and error messages
- Strengthened database protocol packet validation, command controls, and TLS verification
- Improved audit reliability with durable record storage, acknowledgments, retries on failure, and retransmission after restart
- Strengthened verification code protection to prevent codes from appearing in task views or error logs
- Ensured existing SSH keys are disabled after a key reset
- Added support for scheduled rotation of OpenBao access tokens
- Updated FreeRDP to address protocol parsing and memory safety issues
- Enhanced asset connection ACLs to support combinations of request justification, MFA, facial verification, approval, and account operation requirements [JumpServer EE]

## Improvements

- Improved session recording for the desktop client's built-in browser
- Added recording search by window title, with navigation to the corresponding point in the recording
- Enabled NEC to submit recordings to Video Worker for transcoding
- Added support for personal credentials in direct SSH connections
- Refactored the database workbench, migrated the Chen backend to Go, and upgraded the SQL editor to Monaco
- Improved result editing, paginated exports, execution plans, and relationship diagrams in the database workbench
- Improved database transaction control with support for manual commits and rollbacks
- Improved database AI context retrieval with search by table name, column name, and comment
- Refactored the audit report center with configurable sections, report previews, and PDF export
- Improved AI conversation audit queries and permission isolation
- Unified asset and account connectivity testing, with detailed results and execution history
- Improved task management with visibility into queues, worker processes, and logs, along with support for canceling pending tasks and terminating eligible running tasks
- Optimized log queries, audit reports, cloud synchronization, and background tasks to reduce resource overhead
- Optimized RDP recording encoding and memory reclamation
- Improved remote connection settings for printer redirection, security protocols, and Windows key combinations
- Added asset authorization renewal requests based on approved authorization tickets, with new authorization periods granted upon approval [JumpServer EE]
- Improved cloud synchronization status visibility and resource binding tracking with progress, change, and error details, plus a pending-review workflow to prevent assets from being incorrectly released when scans are incomplete [JumpServer EE]

## Bug Fixes

- Fixed issues with database query cancellation, result editing, paginated exports, and connection context
- Fixed session invalidation caused by editing personal credential descriptions
- Fixed issues with job parameter submission, clearing template variables, and editor state after renaming playbooks
- Fixed WebSFTP upload chunk ordering and file retention for download auditing
- Fixed issues with terminal approval confirmation and cancellation, and Vim rendering
- Fixed file retention issues when recording transcoding fails
- Fixed username and email conflicts during concurrent user creation, along with duplicate login logs and email notifications
- Fixed Windows asset list loading failures when the standalone client connects to the Community Edition
- Improved connection compatibility for Oracle SYSDBA, Windows OCI, ClickHouse JDBC/DBeaver, and DBX [JumpServer EE]
- Fixed credential synchronization failures after account provisioning, along with directory service account switching and validation issues [JumpServer EE]
- Fixed issues with ticket approver previews, approval notifications, and legacy rule migration [JumpServer EE]

## Installation and Upgrade

- Upgraded bundled PostgreSQL to 18.7 and Redis to 8.10.3
- Added automatic migration for bundled PostgreSQL 10–17 in standard deployments, preserving existing data, backups, and migration progress, with support for resuming interrupted migrations; external databases and customized deployments are excluded
- Added an email address uniqueness constraint; for existing duplicate addresses, one account retains the original address while the others receive temporary ".invalid" placeholder addresses, and administrators are notified to correct them
- Improved installation and recovery by standardizing component directories, permissions, and key initialization, with better support for legacy Compose versions, executor networking, and service recovery after PostgreSQL upgrades
- Added a 30-second confirmation prompt when a routine database backup fails, with upgrades proceeding by default on timeout; backups for PostgreSQL major version migrations remain mandatory
- Improved high availability upgrades with JDMC coordination of PostgreSQL migrations and Redis updates on both nodes; both JDMC instances must support the migration process before a full upgrade [JumpServer EE]
- Improved high availability recovery, including primary and standby node rejoining, recovery from interrupted node decommissioning, and handling of socket conflicts in shared directories [JumpServer EE]
- JDMC updates require matching Core/Xpack support for the new socket discovery mechanism; environments using the PROXY protocol must configure trusted proxy networks [JumpServer EE]
- Added automatic migration of legacy tickets and workflows; complex approver rules may be disabled pending review [JumpServer EE]
